name: Kerala Mushroom Roast
steps: Clean mushrooms with a damp cloth and halve large ones. Keep them dry so they brown instead of steaming.
Heat 20 ml coconut oil in a wide pan. Cook onions with half the curry leaves for 10 minutes until deep golden. Add ginger, garlic and slit green chilies; stir for 1 minute.
Add coriander, chili powder, turmeric, pepper and crushed fennel. Stir for 30 seconds, then add chopped tomatoes and salt. Cook for 6 minutes until the tomato moisture reduces to a thick masala.
Add mushrooms and spread them across the pan. Cook uncovered over medium-high heat for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring only occasionally, until the water they release evaporates and their edges brown.
Add the remaining 10 ml coconut oil and curry leaves. Roast for 2 minutes more until the masala clings to the mushrooms; serve semi-dry with appam or chapati.
tips: Use a wide pan and avoid crowding it: mushrooms release water, and a Kerala roast should finish with concentrated masala rather than thin gravy.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
